character.name: Archimedes (artistic interpretation)
character.description: A fictional artistic interpretation of Archimedes of Syracuse: a Greek scholar in his early sixties, short neatly trimmed silver beard, thoughtful deep-set eyes, sun-weathered olive skin, silver hair. He wears a cream wool chiton with a deep terracotta himation draped over one shoulder. Dignified, intelligent, warm. Photorealistic, natural skin texture, cinematic lighting.

A_discovery.video_idea: One man only: a fictional artistic interpretation of Archimedes, a Greek scholar in his sixties with silver hair, a short silver beard, cream chiton and terracotta himation; the same man throughout; no other people; do not restyle or recast him. Ancient Syracuse, a stone bath chamber at golden hour. He never looks at the camera and never speaks: he is not a presenter. His eyes stay on the golden laurel crown in his hands, his mouth closed, with a quiet, contemplative expression. He slowly turns the crown in the warm sunlight, studying it, then gently lowers it into the wide bronze basin in front of him, which is filled to the brim; the water rises and visibly spills over the rim in glittering streams. He watches the overflow intently, deep in thought. Tall composition: basin and crown in the lower half, his face in the upper half, centred. Slow, steady camera push-in. Realistic, natural, unhurried movement. Cinematic golden-hour lighting with warm sunbeams and floating dust.
A_discovery.scene_prompt: Ancient Greek stone bath chamber in Syracuse, golden-hour sunlight through limestone columns, warm dust in sunbeams, bronze basin brimming with water, golden laurel crown, photorealistic cinematic film still, shallow depth of field, film grain, no text, no logos

B_realization.video_idea: The same man only, a fictional artistic interpretation of Archimedes with a short silver beard, cream chiton and terracotta himation; no other people; do not restyle or recast him.
